title: Maintain interop sanity matrix for fallback model variants and router preflight checks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: The smart routing layer can fall back to variant models across regions and tiers. We must ensure tokenizer parity, context-window compatibility, and runtime/tooling invariants (KV cache keys, attention cache formats, and sampling seeds) so that a routed fallback does not cause correctness regressions or runtime failures. This ticket is to maintain the canonical compatibility matrix, automate detection of drift, and surface preflight checks to the router so incompatible variants are not used as fallbacks.

Goals:
- Stabilize the compatibility matrix (format: JSON schema stored in infra/config/variant-interop.json) and add strict CI validation on model onboarding PRs.
- Implement nightly sweep job that detects tokenizer/model artifacts changes and flags compatibility deltas.
- Add router preflight gating: a lightweight compatibility check before routing to a fallback variant (tokenizer ID, max_context, kv-format version).
- Provide a test harness (e2e) that runs 200 canonical prompts across primary+fallback pairs to detect behavioral drift.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: tokenizer ID parity, context limit compatibility, KV cache ABI, seed/temperature mapping, and tooling flags required for function calling. Also update documentation and console visibility.
- Non-goal: retraining or fine-tuning models. Not in scope: changing model serving kernels or quantization profiles (separate runtime work).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Store matrix as a single source-of-truth JSON in infra config to make lookup O(1) from router. This increases coupling between infra and router but provides simple, auditable rules.
- Nightly sweep uses a checksum + heuristic diff for tokenizers: exact tokenizer bytehash match => compatible; different but same tokenizer-vocab-version => likely compatible but require sampling regression check. This reduces false positives but still flags potential behavioral differences for manual review.
- Router preflight is intentionally conservative: only route to fallback if explicit compatibility entry exists or automated sweep has a green status. Otherwise route to higher-tier or region fallback as policy. This trades some availability for correctness.

Acceptance criteria:
- The compat matrix JSON schema and validation are merged to infra repo and enforced in CI (infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1473).
- Nightly sweep job implemented in jobs/variant-compat-sweeper and visible on the infra dashboard (Grafana board ID: infra-variant-compat).
- Router preflight implemented with unit tests and integration tests; router rejects fallback routing when compatibility missing and logs reason to tracing.
- e2e harness with 200 prompts runs in CI and produces a behavioral-delta report; CI fails on high divergence (>5% metric regression on BLEU/ROUGE-like signals used for sanity).
- Documentation updated: Confluence doc updated at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Variant+Interop+Sanity+Matrix and UI shows compat status per model in Console > Models > Compatibility.

Testing plan:
1) Unit tests for matrix loader, schema validation, and router preflight logic.
2) Integration test that spins up primary & fallback variant containers (mocked runtime) and asserts tokenizer/context compatibility checks short-circuit incorrect fallbacks.
3) Nightly sweep runs that compare tokenizer hashes and a sampling regression test against cached golden outputs.
4) Canary rollout: enable router preflight for 10% of traffic in staging, monitor errors, and gradually roll to 100% after 72 hours of stable signals.

Risks and mitigation:
- False positives from tokenizer heuristics causing unnecessary route avoidance -> mitigation: add manual override capability in console and rapid remediation workflow.
- Nightly sweep breakage due to upstream model artifact repo changes -> mitigation: pin artifact API version and add alerting on feed failures.
- Performance overhead in router preflight -> mitigation: keep check minimal (tokenizer id and max_context) and cache results in-memory with TTL.

Owners and reviewers:
- Owner: Liam O'Connell (runtime infra)
- Reviewer: Priya Rao (serving runtime), Ben Carter (router), and Ana Gonzalez (QA)

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Variant+Interop+Sanity+Matrix
- Infra PR (validation + schema): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1473
- Jobs PR (sweeper): https://github.com/redwood-inference/jobs/pull/221
- Router PR (preflight): https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/562

Notes: This ticket complements ENG-81234 (router rollout policy) and ENG-80001 (model onboarding pipeline). The matrix should be reviewed by model oncall and runtime oncall weekly during the first month after rollout.
updates: 2026-03-10 - Ticket created by Maya Patel with initial design notes and scope.
2026-03-11 - Spike completed: tokenizer hash heuristic prototype implemented. Found 3 models with identical vocab ID but different byte-hash; added secondary sampling check requirement.
2026-03-12 - Infra schema PR opened (infra/pull/1473). CI failing on schema edge cases for ensemble models; fixed and pushed.
2026-03-13 - Router preflight prototype added to feature branch. Early perf numbers: additional latency ~0.6ms p95 when cache warm. Decided to use in-memory TTL cache to minimize cost.
2026-03-14 - e2e harness skeleton merged to interop-tests and a first smoke run (20 prompts) passed against staging variants. Next: expand to 200 prompts and add regression thresholding.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix stored and schema-validated in infra repo and protected by CI.
Nightly sweep job detects artifact drift and posts issues when compatibility changes.
Router preflight prevents routing to flagged incompatible fallbacks and logs reasons.
E2E harness covers 200 canonical prompts and CI enforces regression thresholds.
Console shows compatibility state per model variant and provides manual override with audit log.
